title: Early Austin Infrastructure & Safety Upgrades
summary:
• **Railroad Safety Priority**: Council approved automatic warning bells at railroad crossings and new duties for street car conductors at intersections to prevent accidents—addressing growing transportation concerns in the city.

• **West 6th Street Paving Project**: Council awarded a paving contract to the William I. Heffron Company at $2.20 per square yard (lowest bid), allocating $500 for the street improvement project.

• **Health Inspector Appointment Confirmed**: Dr. H.W. Stroter was officially confirmed as City Health Inspector with salary authorization dating back to July 1908.

• **Budget Allocations**: Council approved $1,400 for street department salaries, $300 for extra street labor, and $150 for approved accounts—essential spending to maintain city operations.

• **Employee Standards**: New ordinance passed establishing qualification requirements for regular city employees, formalizing hiring practices.

Committee,beg leave to report that bids for paving West sixth street from the alley west
of Congress Avenue to the west side of Guadalupe street were opened at noon today,as
follows : St John & Roy,paving and excavation,per square yard $2,298 Knox & Johnson paving
and excavation per square yard .2,213 Wm.I Heffron Co Galveston,paving and excavation per
square yard $ 2,20 A bid was also received after meeting adjourned from the General Supply
& Construction Co.,Fort Worth,for $ 2,30 per square yard .
Wm I Heffron Company being the lowest bidders,we recommend the acceptance of their bid,and
that the Mayor be authorized to enter into a contract with them.
